Thanks for the demo today, Marissa — really helpful. A quick recap and a few follow-ups from our side: 

- Goal: Reduce hallucinations in customer-facing search while keeping latency < 300ms on short queries. Target is 95% grounding for top-1 answer on our FAQ/testset.
- Current infra: Elasticsearch + lightweight semantic embeddings (stored in FAISS); first-pass BM25 + vector retrieval.

Immediate questions:
1) Which model(s) would you recommend for our RAG stack (tradeoffs between cost/latency/grounding)?
2) For retriever: do you suggest we keep BM25 first-pass + dense retriever, or move to dense-only? Top_k settings?
3) Reranker: should we use a cross-encoder reranker vs a lightweight score-based reranker? Any recommended architectures?
4) Any benchmark artifacts (prompt sets, eval metrics) you can share so our ML folks can review?

We have a short internal budget review on Friday; if you can get a recommended configuration + rough cost estimate and any benchmark links by Thursday EOD, that would help.

Thanks — Alex

Alex — great follow-up, and appreciate the clear targets. Short answers up front, then a recommended config and attached artifacts.

TL;DR recommendations (based on your goals):
- Model recommendations (ranked):
  1) Redwood-14B-32k (quantized q4f16) — best balance of grounding + instruction-following; good for longer context and fewer retrieval failures. Expect ~10-15% higher cost vs smaller models but better grounding precision.
  2) Llama2-13B-chat or Mistral-7B-Instruct (for lower-cost / lower-latency pilot). These will be cheaper, lower latency, but expect a small drop in grounding precision — mitigations below.
  3) Redwood-7B-low-latency (8k) — if you need strict latency <200ms at scale; pair with aggressive reranker.

- Retriever recommendation:
  - Keep BM25 as a fast first-pass (hybrid approach) + dense retriever (embedding-based) for semantic matches. First-pass BM25 top_k=200, dense retriever top_k=100, then dedupe+merge and pass top_k=10 to the reranker.
  - Use FAISS HNSW for ANN with IVF/OPQ for large corpora (we can help tune).

- Reranker recommendation:
  - Use a lightweight cross-encoder reranker (MiniLM cross-encoder or a fine-tuned DistilBERT cross-encoder) for best grounding precision on top_k=10. If latency is a constraint, use a two-stage reranker: score-based lightweight reranker to cut to top5, then cross-encoder for final.

- Grounding / evaluation metrics to track (we include these in the attached benchmark PDF):
  - precision@1 (is top-1 supported by source?)
  - grounding_rate (fraction of answers citing a supporting doc/passage)
  - hallucination_rate (automatically flagged; requires manual review samples)
  - exact_match_on_facts (for structured queries)
  - latency P95 and cost-per-1k-requests by model variant

Attachments and links: attached prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v2.xlsx) + our benchmark PDF (redwood_benchmark_results_20270614.pdf). Also sharing a retriever config stub (retriever_config_stub.json) in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink

Quality regression notes:
- If you quantize larger models aggressively (q4_0 -> q4f16) you may see subtle regressions on grounding; we recommend running the 500-sample human eval subset in the prompt set before rolling out any quantized model.
- Reranker training: if you fine-tune the cross-encoder on ACME-labeled pairs (we can help with a small 5k-pair seed), you should see a 6-12% relative lift in precision@1.

Rough cost/latency estimate (pilot scale, 10k qps-months):
- Redwood-14B-32k (q4f16): expected latency median ~220-320ms, cost ~ $X / 1k requests (detailed estimate attached).
- Llama2-13B-chat: latency ~180-260ms, lower cost but ~5-10% lower grounding.

Next steps we recommend this week:
1) We (Redwood) run a 1k-sample benchmark on your live index with Redwood-14B-32k + current retriever (no cost if you provide a snapshot export).
2) Your team runs the 500-sample human eval from the attached prompt set to baseline existing grounding rate.
3) Schedule a 60-min tech session next week for retriever/FAISS tuning and reranker fine-tuning priorities.

Can you confirm if you can share a snapshot export (doc ids + text + metadata) and whether your procurement team needs an SOW/PO before we start the pilot?

Cheers,
